correction_2026_10_09: SEPARATOR CORRECTION, 2026-10-09. Every row in this file that spelled a binding `<callable>#<binding>` now spells it with `BINDING_SEP` as the family defines it — U+0000, written `\u0000` in JSON. The character was `#` until src/ast/types.ts commit c95c8485f ("the binding separator was `#` — a character nine lanes legitimately publish, so their claims were unverifiable"): `#` is a real key character in other lanes (a CSS id selector, a markdown label, an HCL address), so `verifyBindingClaim` had to reject every binding claim on a run that also published one. The edges, their lines, their confidence and their metadata are UNCHANGED; only the separator character moved. Measured before this correction: `npx tsx script/m14/run-fixtures.ts --lang dart` -> {"dart":{"pass":21,"fail":7}}, and all 7 failures were rows whose sole difference was this character. Any `#` still visible in this file's prose is the 2026-10-08 spelling quoted as history, not the current one.
authoredNote: Transcribed from a measured run (script/m14/tmp/dt-fixture-dump.ts) against this file. This file is the READING half of a TWO-FILE fixture: `declares.dart` sits beside it and declares an unrelated `Telemetry.counter`, which is what makes the forbid row below a statement about a real collision rather than a hypothetical one. The pair lives in a subdirectory, so the harness treats the two files as one project and every member of it carries its own expectation file (script/m14/run-fixtures.ts enumerates sub-directory members as fixtures).
rationale: PINS THE SPELLING OF A BINDING, which is the half the whole-corpus gate cannot check and the store cannot report. The family contract publishes no locals, parameters or lambda parameters as symbols (DARTD8), so a read of one has no declaration to name — but the analyzer must still say WHICH binding it read, and the string it writes is what the store resolves: `parallel-indexer.resolveRelationships` matches a target against `qualified_name` (Strategy 1) and then against a bare `name` admitted only while the name is declared exactly once in the project (Strategy 2), and it never reads the edge's metadata. A bare local name is therefore indistinguishable from a declaration's name, and `Telemetry.counter` in the sibling file is exactly the collision that turns the read into a false dependency (`local-read-phantom.ts` reproduces it with the store's own rule and shows the binding resolving to an unrelated class's field). The target is `run` + `BINDING_SEP` + `counter` — the enclosing callable, the separator, and the binding's own name — and it carries `localBinding` so the arbiter can check the claim against its OWN key space (`verifyBindingClaim`). The separator was written `#` here when this fixture was authored on 2026-10-08 and has been U+0000 since commit c95c8485f; the row below carries the current spelling and `correction_2026_10_09` records the change with its measurement. The forbid row is the pre-2026-10-08 spelling: it is fireable in the exact shape a revert would produce, which is the form this programme requires of a forbid after finding a fixture whose forbids could not fire at all.

expectRelationships.comment: the read of the function's OWN local: `#` not `.`, because a dot would make the target a member spelling the store would try to bind, and the consumers' leaf rule (after the last colon, then after the last dot) would reduce it back to the bare name

forbidRelationships.note: THE PRE-2026-10-08 SPELLING, and the one the store misbinds: `Telemetry.counter` in the sibling file is the only declaration of that name in the project, so a bare `counter` target resolves to it (Strategy 2, metadata unread) and the stored row asserts that `run` depends on an unrelated class's field. A revert to the bare spelling must fail here, not merely stop being counted.
